stories.title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
summary: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities.
Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers.

stories.title: Deep beneath Australia, hidden caves could unlock the secrets of alien worlds
summary: Scientists have solved the mystery of strange trenches scattered across Australia’s vast Nullarbor Plain, revealing an extensive hidden world beneath the surface.
These subtle landscape features are created as deeply buried cave systems slowly collapse upward over millions of years.
The discovery could help researchers locate unexplored caves containing ancient environmental records and unusual life forms.

stories.title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
summary: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades.
Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile.
The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water.

stories.title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish
summary: The comedian warns extinction beckons for Arctic charr in Windermere after thousands of years.

stories.title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
summary: More than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea, scientists have discovered rare underwater lakes that could reveal secrets about Earth's ancient oceans and the possibility of alien life.
Known as brine pools, these extremely salty, oxygen-free environments are surprisingly teeming with microbial life, challenging our understanding of where living organisms can survive.

stories.title: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars
summary: A mysterious object named Phoebe, detected when it briefly magnified a distant star, could be a primordial black hole formed just after the Big Bang.
With an estimated mass only three times that of the Moon, it may be a 13-billion-year-old cosmic relic that offers new clues to the mystery of dark matter.

stories.title: What UK season changes mean for you
summary: Frosts will become less common and hot summer days more frequent in the UK, the Met Office says.

stories.title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office
summary: Changing seasons are affecting wildlife and leading some farmers to grow different crops.

stories.title: Canadian astronaut welcomes baby girl from space station
summary: Joshua Kutryk, currently on his first space mission, is just the fourth astronaut in history to miss the birth of a child while aboard the International Space Station.

stories.title: New York's annual Thanksgiving Parade threatened by approaching storm
summary: Strong winds and heavy rain are expected to impact celebrations across the USA, with the risk that the famous Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade could be impacted.

stories.title: A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected
summary: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, despite being designed to study distant galaxies and the mysteries of the dark Universe.
The icy object is approximately 1.3 billion kilometers from Earth and follows an unusual orbit that takes thousands of years to complete.

stories.title: Why has China sent the first Pakistani astronaut to space?
summary: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first foreign national to board China's Tiangong space station.

stories.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
summary: Positrons are the antimatter counterpart of an electron.
Positron is suspended in a wall-free trap, safely separated from ordinary matter.
Any difference between the electron and positron could expose cracks in the Standard Model of particle physics.

stories.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals.
Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought.
Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.

summary: The council says the 20-tonne pile of rubbish was dumped over garden fences.

stories.title: China's Shenzhou-24 carries Pakistan's first astronaut into space
